matchstick.title: Compute numeric values and discrepancy
matchstick.principle: Convert each Roman numeral in the equation to its integer value and compute the difference between the two sides; this guides which stick moves could balance the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: At the start of solving a matchstick puzzle, before considering any stick moves.
matchstick.example: Assuming the equation is correct without calculating that XI = 11 and II - IX = -7.

matchstick.title: List possible single‑stick transformations
matchstick.principle: Enumerate every way a single matchstick can be relocated from any character (including operators) to any other character, ensuring both source and destination remain valid symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After computing the numeric discrepancy, to generate candidate moves.
matchstick.example: Overlooking the possibility of moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-' to swap the operators.

matchstick.title: Match numeric difference to value change
matchstick.principle: For each candidate stick move, calculate how the numeric values of the affected numerals change and check whether the resulting equation balances.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After generating candidate moves, to filter those that could resolve the discrepancy.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick that changes XV to XVI but not adjusting III, leaving the numeric difference unchanged.

matchstick.title: Operator modification via plus
matchstick.principle: A '+' consists of one vertical and one horizontal stick; removing the vertical stick leaves a '-', and adding a vertical stick to a '-' creates a '+'.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric discrepancy suggests changing a subtraction to addition or vice versa.
matchstick.example: Adding a vertical stick to '-' to make '+', but taking it from an 'I' that then disappears, making the source character invalid.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑operator stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A stick can be transferred directly from one operator to another, simultaneously altering both operators (e.g., moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-' to swap them).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the needed numeric adjustment can be achieved by changing operator signs rather than numeral values.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-' without ensuring a new '=' appears, resulting in an equation without an equality sign.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑numeral stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If adding a stick to a numeral can increase (or decrease) its value by the needed amount, move a stick from an operator or another numeral to that numeral, ensuring both remain valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When adjusting numeric values by modifying a numeral is more efficient than changing operators.
matchstick.example: Transferring a vertical stick from III to XV to form XVI, but forgetting to remove the stick from III, leaving an extra stick and an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Equation structure preservation
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, the equation must still contain exactly one '=', and each side must have at least one numeral and valid operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After applying a stick move, to verify the structural integrity of the equation.
matchstick.example: Removing the '-' operator entirely, producing 'XI = II IX' which lacks an operator between the numerals.

matchstick.title: Known single‑stick numeral transformations
matchstick.principle: Map common single‑stick changes (e.g., X↔V, I↔V, I↔X) to their numeric value changes (±5, ±4, ±9) and use them to evaluate candidate moves.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When evaluating how moving a stick will affect a numeral's value.
matchstick.example: Changing X to V by removing a diagonal stick, but forgetting that V requires two diagonal sticks, resulting in an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Validate resulting Roman numerals
matchstick.principle: After any stick move that alters a numeral, verify that the resulting numeral follows standard Roman numeral rules (e.g., no more than three consecutive I's, correct subtractive notation).
matchstick.when_to_apply: After generating a candidate transformation, before accepting it as a solution.
matchstick.example: Creating 'IIII' from 'III' by adding a vertical stick, which violates Roman numeral rules.

matchstick.title: Maintain exactly one equality sign after stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When moving a stick from the '=' sign, ensure that another operator becomes '=', so the final equation still contains exactly one equality sign; the original '=' may change to another valid operator (e.g., '-'), but a new '=' must appear elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a candidate move involves the equality sign or could affect the count of '=' signs.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from '=' to '-' without creating a new '=', resulting in an equation with no equality sign.

matchstick.description: Leaving a character invalid after moving a stick
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model moves a stick without checking that the source or destination character remains a valid Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each proposed move, verify that both the character losing the stick and the character gaining the stick still correspond to a valid symbol according to matchstick definitions.

matchstick.description: Failing to verify numeric equality after transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on making the symbols look valid but doesn't compute the resulting numeric values to confirm the equation balances.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Compute the integer values of both sides after each candidate move and only accept moves that make the equation true.

matchstick.description: Dropping or omitting parts of the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: In the process of moving sticks, the model may inadvertently delete an operator or numeral, resulting in an incomplete expression.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure the final equation contains the same number of tokens (numerals and operators) as the original, with exactly one '=', and that no token is missing.

matchstick.description: Ignoring the numeric impact of operator sign change
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model changes an operator (e.g., '-' to '+') without accounting for how this alters the arithmetic result.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: When modifying operators, recalculate the numeric effect of the sign change and verify that it helps resolve the discrepancy.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model either adds or removes sticks instead of relocating exactly one, violating the puzzle rule.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Keep track of the stick count: one stick must be removed from a source character and added to a destination character, with no other changes.
